assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of X-ray, optical and radio afterglows settled a three-decade puzzle by fixing gamma-ray bursts at cosmological distances and opening the way to host-galaxy, redshift and progenitor studies. The discovery is clear, original and tied to a specific observation, and it transformed high-energy astrophysics. As an instrument-driven result it rewards careful detector and satellite work.
assessment.attribution: The BeppoSAX X-ray localisation and afterglow discovery rest on Costa and Frontera, who led the Wide Field Cameras and gamma-ray burst monitor science. Kulkarni's group delivered the first radio afterglow and key follow-up, so the trio is defensible. Other essential contributors, notably the late Jan van Paradijs and the optical-identification teams, fall outside the supplied names, and I cannot independently settle how credit should be split between X-ray and optical discovery.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by hundreds of afterglows over nearly thirty years, linked to supernovae and compact-object mergers, and stable in interpretation. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the supplied names cover the decisive contributors, given that Jan van Paradijs and optical-afterglow teams are absent.
Relative weight of the X-ray discovery versus the optical and redshift follow-up is uncertain to me and not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube observation of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, followed by evidence for TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, created neutrino astronomy as a real observational field. Building a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice was a bold experimental conception with lasting impact on astroparticle physics.
assessment.attribution: Only one name is supplied. Halzen is the central conceptual and project leader of IceCube, but the discovery is the work of a large collaboration, and earlier pioneers of neutrino telescopes and of the AMANDA precursor are not in the credited list, so a single-laureate prize looks narrow. I cannot add names beyond the supplied string.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is established by independent analyses, though source identification is still developing and only partly confirmed by a second experiment. Mature enough for the core discovery, with source physics still maturing.
uncertainties: Individual attribution within a very large collaboration and a decades-long pioneering effort is not resolved.
Source associations beyond the blazar and Galactic plane evidence remain statistically modest and await independent confirmation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea and brought to 10^-18 fractional precision, redefined what measurement can do. It enables tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a prospective redefinition of the second. The principle is clear and the impact lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye drove the performance to the 10^-18 level and broad applications. The pair gives a clean two-person prize configuration. Other groups, notably those working on ion clocks and on lattice clocks elsewhere, are outside the list, so I note that overlap without resolving it.
assessment.maturity: Independent clocks around the world agree at the 10^-18 level, and the technology is mature. Prizes for frequency combs and ion-trap work have already been given, so some of the field is recognised, but the lattice clock remains distinct.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes for precision spectroscopy and ion manipulation may be argued against recognition.
Whether the redefinition of the second will be adopted soon is uncertain and is not evidence of discovery merit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the observation of correlated insulation and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene launched an extremely active field of moire quantum matter. The experimental discovery is striking and originates a platform now generating fractional Chern insulators and other phases.
assessment.attribution: MacDonald and Bistritzer supplied the theoretical flat-band prediction and Jarillo-Herrero led the experimental discovery. I select MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero as a theory-plus-experiment pairing, though Bistritzer's role in the original calculation and the role of the first author of the experimental papers raise unresolved allocation questions.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many independent groups since 2018 and still expanding, but the field is young and the superconducting mechanism is not settled. Recognition is somewhat early but the discovery itself is secure.
uncertainties: Exclusion of Rafi Bistritzer from the proposed set is a debatable judgement about credit for the original theory.
The mechanism of superconductivity and the long-term importance of the platform are still open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection of single nitrogen-vacancy centres and their coherent control created a room-temperature solid-state qubit and a new class of nanoscale quantum sensors with applications from materials science to biology. The discovery is concrete, original and widely used.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup demonstrated optical detection of single spins and Jelezko demonstrated coherent control in the early 2000s, which together form the experimental core. Lukin contributed important sensing proposals and applications but also appears under other candidates; I leave him out to keep the experimental attribution tight, acknowledging that the sensing theory credit is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many groups and commercial development, with stable interpretation. The sensing applications keep evolving, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Whether quantum sensing proposals deserve separate recognition and how credit divides with Lukin and others is uncertain.
Overlap with candidate B033 on optical access to single spins could complicate a combined prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for ion-trap quantum gates and Blatt's experimental realisation of entangling operations and algorithms established trapped ions as a leading platform for quantum computation and simulation. The work is original and has had lasting impact on quantum information science.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the decisive theoretical proposal and Blatt delivered key experiments, giving a natural theory-plus-experiment trio. Wineland's group also contributed, but he is recognised separately and is not in the supplied credit, so the allocation cannot be fully assessed here.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed across several independent laboratories and now commercial systems, though scalable fault-tolerant computing is not yet shown. Recognition is reasonable but part of the quantum-control field has already been honoured.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with other quantum-computing platforms may affect priority.
Final importance depends on how scalable quantum computing develops.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP delivered precision maps of the microwave background that fixed cosmological parameters at the percent level and established the standard model of cosmology. It is a landmark instrument-based measurement with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission as principal investigator, Page was central to instrument design and calibration, and Spergel to the cosmological analysis. The trio is workable, but a large collaboration contributed, and the COBE prize and Planck follow-up complicate how the unique contribution is defined.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed and extended by Planck and ground-based experiments, so the maturity is high. Recognition risk is that the field has already been honoured for COBE and for the accelerating universe.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views WMAP as a distinct discovery or as a refinement of earlier recognised work.
Credit among many collaboration members and the choice of names is not fully verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The conception and construction of ATLAS and CMS enabled the discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012, one of the central experimental achievements of particle physics, which complements the 2013 prize for the theoretical prediction. The detector concepts and their delivery had a profound and lasting effect.
assessment.attribution: Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are recognised as leading figures in the proposal and construction of the two experiments, an unusual instrument-focused credit that fits an experimental prize for a detector-enabled discovery. Recognising a few individuals for collaborations of thousands is delicate, and analysis leadership is excluded from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: The Higgs discovery is confirmed with extensive follow-up measurements, so maturity is high. The issue is the unusual attribution, not the science.
uncertainties: Recognising spokespeople and project leaders rather than analysis leaders is contentious and could be seen as incomplete.
Whether the committee would prefer a prize for the discovery itself rather than the instrument construction remains open.
